verses.text: Then the prophets Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo spoke God's messages to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem. They spoke in the name of the God of Israel, who was over them.
So Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak started again to build God's temple in Jerusalem. The prophets of God were with them, helping them.

At that time Tattenai, the governor of the land west of the Euphrates River, Shethar-Bozenai, and their friends came to them and asked, "Who gave you permission to rebuild this temple and finish this wall?"
They also asked, "What are the names of the men working on this building?"
But God was watching over the leaders of the Jews. So the officials did not stop them until a report could be sent to Darius and an answer came back in a letter.
This is a copy of the letter that Tattenai, the governor of the land west of the Euphrates River, Shethar-Bozenai, and their friends, the officials west of the river, sent to King Darius.
The report they sent said: "To King Darius: Greetings and peace.

The king should know that we went to the province of Judah, to the temple of the great God. It is being built with large stones, and wooden beams are being put in the walls. The work is being done with great care and is going well.
We asked the leaders, 'Who gave you permission to rebuild this temple and finish this wall?'
We also asked their names, so that we could write down the names of their leaders for you.
This is the answer they gave us: 'We are servants of the God of heaven and earth. We are rebuilding the temple that was built many years ago. A great king of Israel built it and finished it.
But our ancestors made the God of heaven angry, so he handed them over to Nebuchadnezzar the Babylonian, king of Babylon. He destroyed this temple and took the people away to Babylon.
But in the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon, King Cyrus gave an order to rebuild this temple of God.

King Cyrus also took out of the temple in Babylon the gold and silver things from God's temple, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem and brought to the temple in Babylon. He gave them to a man named Sheshbazzar, whom he had made governor.
Cyrus told him, "Take these things and put them back in the temple in Jerusalem. Rebuild God's temple on its old site."
So Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of God's temple in Jerusalem. Since then it has been under construction, but it is not finished yet.'

Now, if it pleases the king, let a search be made in the royal records in Babylon. See if King Cyrus really gave an order to rebuild this temple of God in Jerusalem. Then let the king send us his decision about this."
